title: feat(sync-in): every pull leaves a sys_sync_run row, and a datasource pull reads on from the position the last run committed (ADR-0153 D7)
body:
Part of #32062

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: semantic
Skills-docs: none — no published skill teaches `connectorSource`, `datasourceSource` or `sys_sync_run` today (`git grep` over `skills/` finds none); the hand-written guide this change made false, `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx` ("Pulling a mapping"), is corrected in this PR, and the sync-in guide and skills are ADR-0153's P3 guide + skills child

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：每次拉取（job 的 `pull`，连接器源或数据源源）都会在新的平台对象 `sys_sync_run` 里留一行运行记录：读了哪里、读写了多少、提交到哪个读取位置、怎么结束。数据源拉取在每个窗口读完时把读取位置存进这行，下一次拉取从那里接着读，不再每次从 `watermark.start` 全量重读。
- 为什么改：ADR-0153 D7 和不变式 8、9；席位在 6782048815 把它定为第三片。第二片披露过的“每次运行都改写每一行”（记录自动化、审计行、`updated_at` 每次都动）到这一片结束。
- 风险与回滚：运行记录写不进去时拉取会被拒绝（`run_record_unavailable`，503），不会静默地退回全量重读；没有数据引擎或 manifest 服务的组合照旧运行，只是不记位置，启动后第一次拉取时警告一次。服务器停机时留下的 `running` 行在下次启动时关成 `failed`（`interrupted`），已提交的位置保留。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-run-ledger.ts`（位置的读、写与交接）、`datasource-pull.ts` 的起点选择（`lastCommitted`、`full`、同源同字段判断）、`connector-pull.ts` 的 `openSyncRun` / `closeFailedRun`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/datasource-pull.test.ts`，预期全绿，含“窗口中途停下只提交到上一个读完的窗口，下次从那里接着读”的用例。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

Slice 3 of the sync-in P2 engine, scoped by the seat in 6782048815 (ADR-0153 D7, invariants 8 and 9), after #32073 closed.

- **The run record, `sys_sync_run`** (`packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-sync-run.object.ts`), registered beside `sys_automation_run` in the automation plugin's manifest (answer 3 of 6773389044), and with the credential objects under `suspendedRunStore: 'memory'`, because a read position needs its table whatever the suspended-run store is. Organization-owned (ADR-0131), engine-owned, reads open through the data API (`get`, `list`). One row per pull: the organization, mapping, source kind, source (the federated object or the connector), datasource, read path, watermark field, where the read started, the counts (read, created, updated, refused), the committed position and when it was committed, status (`running` / `completed` / `degraded` / `failed`), start and end, and the failure (`failure_reason`, the platform's sentence; never a driver's or an upstream's own text).
- **The writer** (`sync-run-ledger.ts`, `ObjectStoreSyncRunLedger`). `pullConnectorSource` opens a run before it reads the mapping and closes it when the pull ends, for either source, so a refused pull is a `failed` run with the refusal's `reason`. A run is scoped by the organization its row holds, read back once at open: under `single` the engine stamps the Default Organization on a run written with none (ADR-0131 D10), and a scope re-derived from the job's context would miss the row (measured: a `$null` predicate matched nothing).
- **The committed position (invariants 8 and 9).** The window reader's `commit` hook, a no-op since slice 1, now stores the position at each window's end. A datasource pull starts from the position the latest committed run of the mapping in its organization stored, when that run read the same source object on the same `watermark.field`, and never below `watermark.start`. A first run, a run with `full: true`, and a run whose stored position came from another source or field start at `watermark.start`. This makes the contract's `watermark.committed` wording true (slice-2 review N3); the contract text is unchanged.
- **Retention.** `lifecycle: { class: 'telemetry', retention: { maxAge: '30d', onlyWhen: { status: { $in: ['completed', 'degraded', 'failed'] }, holds_position: false } } }`: the job ledger's window, never shorter (D7). The open point ADR-0153 leaves to this card ("how the sweep keeps" the latest committed run) is decided as a declared row filter: the writer keeps `holds_position` true on the run of a mapping and organization committed last, and the one platform sweep exempts it, with every `running` row. Every commit sets its own row's flag first, then clears it on rows of the scope committed earlier (`committed_at` below its own): a crash between the two writes keeps both, never neither, and two runs of one mapping that interleave their windows each clear the other only when it is older, so the run committed last keeps the flag.
- **The end-of-pull log line.** One line when a pull ends: `info` with the counts, the committed position and the run id, or the existing `warn` (now worded for either source) with the refusal and the counts so far.
- **The interrupted-run close.** The plugin's `start()` closes every `running` row `failed` with `failure_reason: 'interrupted'`; the committed position stands. In a cluster a run still live on another replica is closed too: its own end rewrites the row, and the position is read by commit time, never by status, so the next pull's starting point is the same either way.
- **A new refusal reason, `run_record_unavailable`** (`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, 503): the run cannot be opened (nothing is read), the last position cannot be read (the pull does not start), or a position cannot be stored at a window's end (the windows before stay written). A composition with no ledger (no data engine, no manifest service) runs as before, keeps no position, and says so once at `warn`.
- **`full` is live.** `datasourceSource.full` flips `planned` → `live` and its `authorWarn` is dropped; the container and `watermark.start` rows say where a run starts now.
- **Registries the new platform object joins:** `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['service-automation']` (`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`, the one `packages/spec/src` hunk, named in the report: its maintenance contract requires the name of every object the package registers), the tenancy census (regenerated, in reach on `organization_id`), and the CLI organization-ownership inventory (fate `attribution`, as `sys_connector_connection`).
- **Docs and changesets.** `jobs.mdx` ("Pulling a mapping") says where a run starts and what the run record holds. DELIBERATE CORRECTION of the unreleased slice-2 changeset `.changeset/32062-sync-in-datasource-pull.md`: its note "**No committed position is kept yet.** … every run rewrites every row of the `synced` target …" becomes "**Where a run starts.** Each run reads on from the read position the last run of the mapping committed, stored on `sys_sync_run` (ADR-0153 D7, in the same release: see its own entry), so it reads only the rows written since, plus the rows sharing that position, which the keyed upsert writes again harmlessly. The first run, and every run of a mapping that declares `full: true`, reads from `watermark.start`. `deletePolicy` and `deletedField` still warn their author that they change nothing yet." Both changesets ship in one release, so the old sentence would contradict the new entry.

## Tests

- `datasource-pull.test.ts`, on a real engine (SQLite target, federated SQLite source), new top-level describes:
  - a completed pull leaves one row with its source, counts, committed position and the holder flag, and logs exactly one end line;
  - a pull refused before the mapping is read is a `failed` run with the refusal's reason and sentence;
  - a second run after a committed first run starts at the committed position: every window read is bounded below at it, a row below it is not read again, a row sharing it is;
  - a run stopped mid-window (the remote fails on the second page of the second window) keeps window 1's position, keeps the driver's text off the record, and the next run reads on from there;
  - a run a stopped server left `running` is closed `failed` / `interrupted` by the boot close, its position stands, and the next pull starts there; a second boot closes nothing;
  - `full: true` reads from `watermark.start` every run; a stored position from another watermark field is not used;
  - two runs of one mapping committing in turn: the run committed last holds the position, and it is the one the next pull reads;
  - `run_record_unavailable` on open (nothing read) and on a window's commit (the earlier window's position stands);
  - retention through the real Reaper (`LifecycleService` over live SQLite): one sweep past the window deletes the superseded run and keeps the position holder and a `running` row.
- `plugin-suspended-run-wiring.test.ts`: the boot close runs once at `start()` in both store modes and not when the object never reached a manifest; a pull through the plugin opens and closes a run row.
- `activation-ledger-registration.test.ts`, `plugin-suspended-run-wiring.test.ts`: the registered-object pins name `sys_sync_run`.

## Acceptance notes

- Not recorded yet, each needing more than this slice may touch: the `sys_job_run` id and the trigger (`schedule` / `manual`) D7 lists. The job handler is invoked with `{ jobId, data }` only (`JobHandler`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/job-service.ts`), so carrying the run id needs that contract widened and the `service-job` adapters to pass it, and the claim keeps `service-job` to D8. Raised as an open question in the report. The marked-deleted and NULL-watermark counts land with D3.
- A connector source keeps reading its starting point from its target (W1). Its one commit after the last page is D2's connector paging loop, a later slice.
- Studio's run history view is the P3 Studio child.
- The `committed_at` guard on the hand-over matters only when two runs' writes interleave between a commit's two updates. A sequential test cannot order them, so no test pins the guard itself; the per-commit hand-over it protects is pinned (the two-runs case).
- The boot close runs once per plugin start over every `running` row. In a cluster that includes a run still live on another replica; its own end rewrites the row (described in What changes).
- Every pull still logs its existing start line beside the one end line; D7 asks for the end line, and the start line was not removed.

## Verification

objectstack-ai/objectstack, branch recreated from `origin/main` `84aabea5` after #32339 landed; `origin/main` merged three times while this slice was verified (`326453eb`, `a0e2d776`, `91d88ec1`), the last one bringing #32294, which edits the same pull files (resolved below). Final head `2b35e25a`.

<details><summary>The merge with #32294</summary>

#32294 (a job's connector pull reads its mapping from the job's package, ADR-0150 D3) landed on `main` while this slice was in verification and changed `connector-pull.ts`, `plugin.ts`, `pull-refusal.ts` and `jobs.mdx`. Three textual conflicts, each resolved by keeping both sides:

- `ConnectorPullDeps` carries both `mappingByPackage` (#32294) and `runs` (this slice);
- the plugin's pull passes both;
- `jobs.mdx` keeps #32294's "Which mapping a name reads" text and this slice's run-record sentences.

#32294's package-scoped mapping read runs inside `pullOnce`, which now runs inside the run record, so its refusals are `failed` runs like every other. #32294's new tests pass on the merged head (service-automation 3728 tests, up from 3714).

</details>

<details><summary>Tests and typecheck</summary>

- Build closures, each `VERDICT command-exit 0`: `@objectstack/service-automation^...` (first), then after each merge `@objectstack/service-automation...`, `@objectstack/runtime...`, `@objectstack/cli...`, `@objectstack/client-react...`, `@objectstack/dogfood^...` and the five packages `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` reads.
- On `26b27ac9` (the merge with #32294; the final head adds only `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`):
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation typecheck`: exit 0, `check:test-typecheck` OK; `pnpm test`: Test Files 275 passed (275), Tests 3728 passed (3728);
  - `packages/runtime` `src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts`: 38 / 38;
  - `packages/cli` `src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.test.ts`: 26 / 26.
- On `14e042ff`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck` OK); the CLI `unit` layer 412 / 412 files (5887 tests). Two files there (`published-subpath-console.pin`, `published-subpath-hook-body.pin`) first refused because `packages/cli` itself was not built, and passed 29 / 29 once it was.
- `packages/spec` `src/system/constants/platform-object-names.test.ts`: 14 / 14. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: after `gen:liveness-counts` (the mapping counts move with `full`), every artifact current. Its `check:test-typecheck` leg crashed with no diagnostics at the default heap while other work ran, and passed at `--max-old-space-size=8192` (52 files / 240 errors / 131 pinned signatures held). That is the memory crash slice 1 reported, not a stale ledger.
- The first full service-automation run failed one pin, `admin-copy-vocabulary.test.ts`: two `sys_sync_run` field descriptions carried an ADR id. They were rewritten, and the ids moved into the comments.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations — one per pinned behaviour, each red, each restored byte-exact</summary>

On `14e042ff`, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 → 0, restored blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty), running `datasource-pull.test.ts` and `plugin-suspended-run-wiring.test.ts` (40 tests; every subject resolves from source):

1. Resume: `from` always `watermark.start`: 3 failed (the second run, the mid-window stop, the boot close).
2. The commit hook stores nothing: 5 failed.
3. `full: true` ignored: 1 failed.
4. A stored position from another source or field used: 1 failed.
5. The run scoped by the asked organization, not the stored one: 5 failed.
6. The holder hand-over never clears an earlier holder: 3 failed.
7. Retention's `holds_position: false` exemption dropped: 1 failed (the holder is swept).
8. The plugin's boot close not called: 3 failed.
9. The end line logged at `debug`: 1 failed.
10. The driver's message written to the record: 1 failed.
11. A failed commit thrown raw, not `run_record_unavailable`: 1 failed.
12. The boot close matching no `running` row: 3 failed.

</details>

<details><summary>Gates</summary>

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 129 families from the PR's 21 paths at `2b35e25a`, and all 129 ran there. 128 exit 0. `check-empty-changeset` exits 1, and that is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION declared under What changes. The gate's own text: "declare the DELIBERATE CORRECTION on the PR, naming each note and quoting the corrected sentences … this gate stays red either way". It is confirmed by the seat's record, not routed around.
- A worker restart stopped the run after family 29. It resumed at family 30 on the same head, with an unchanged tree.
- `--ran` with recorded exit codes: "129 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 129 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 129 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)".
- Found by the union on earlier heads, and fixed:
  - the tenant-audit census: the ledger adds six write call sites, so it was regenerated, and the census page's hand-written figures moved with it (300 to 306 sites, 207 to 213 decidable, 166 to 172 elevated, 79 to 85 named through a `const`);
  - the engine-double ledger: the retention pin's sweep engine was recorded with `--write`;
  - the liveness evidence of `full`: it cited a file that never names the key.
- `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first refused with PREREQUISITE NOT MET, for want of built packages. They ran after the builds they read.
- Not run locally: `pnpm lint` and the rest of the CI farm, which CI owns. Dogfood battery: not owed, since the title carries no `!` and the Clause-② line carries the widening arm.

</details>
